scope.note: All mappings below were checked against the local PDF body. E3 labels are survey conventions, not quotations or definitions attributed to the paper authors.

evidence_levels.E2: Supported by the reported method or experimental design, but not stated in exactly this survey terminology.
evidence_levels.E3: Survey-level normalization introduced to compare heterogeneous papers.
evidence_levels.E4: Not reported clearly enough in the PDF to verify.

evidence.claim: The paper distinguishes a tool as a self-contained function and a skill as a structured multi-file package, and co-evolves a skill generator with a surrogate verifier.
SkillsBench contains 85 tasks and the ground-truth oracle is exposed as an opaque pass/fail signal rather than test content.
The evolved package is evaluated with Claude Code and Codex, including portability experiments.
SP→SU + EV is a normalization of the paper's multi-file skill-package and verifier co-evolution, not the authors' ontology.

papers.claim_boundary: Supports package generation, verification and portability. It does not by itself establish skill-collection scaling or retrieval quality.

evidence.claim: The model remains frozen while structured reusable skill folders are proposed, refined and accumulated.
Failure diagnosis can compare the agent answer with the ground-truth answer, and train, validation and held-out test subsets are disjoint.
The paper reports zero-shot transfer from SealQA skills to BrowseComp.
SU/SC separates the individual generated folder from the accumulated repository; the paper does not use this ontology.

papers.claim_boundary: Comparable to frozen external-skill methods only when ground-truth diagnosis and validation-query budgets are matched.

papers.carrier: text prompts and compound-system program components

evidence.claim: GEPA is introduced as a reflective prompt optimizer and compared with prompt optimization and reinforcement-learning baselines.
Training text and labels are available to the optimizer, while validation access is restricted to evaluation signals under the stated protocol.
Experiments include AIME, LiveBench-Math, HotpotQA, IFBench, HoVer and PUPA, with comparisons including GRPO, MIPROv2 and TextGrad.
Prompt/Program is kept as a separate track because the primary optimized state is not an external skill collection.

papers.claim_boundary: A relevant optimization baseline, but not a direct member of an external skill-acquisition leaderboard.

evidence.claim: The method separates task-skill evolution from meta-skill evolution and uses a shared frozen backbone.
Task skills are updated on a fast timescale and Analyzer, Retriever, Allocator, Proposer and Evolver behavior is updated on a slow timescale.
OfficeQA, SealQA and ALFWorld are evaluated on held-out splits.
meta-SU/process records that the meta components are both reusable procedural controllers and part of the evolution algorithm.

papers.claim_boundary: Extra meta-agent calls and two-timescale update opportunities must be counted before comparison with single-level skill rewriting.

papers.carrier: model parameters with temporary skill context

evidence.claim: The stated goal is to internalize structured skill packages into the model and progressively withdraw skill context during training.
Experiments cover ALFWorld, search-based QA and WebShop and update model parameters.
Search QA distinguishes in-domain datasets from out-of-domain datasets.
PP denotes parameter/policy state and prevents the named SkillBank from being treated as a separate ontology.

papers.claim_boundary: Must be evaluated as skill-assisted parameter learning, not directly ranked against frozen external-skill methods.

evidence.claim: The base model is frozen and the method localizes the first actionable failure step before attributing responsibility to candidate skills.
Evaluation uses WebShop, PinchBench and Claw-Eval, including the OpenClaw runtime.
The main intervention is local maintenance of an existing skill collection rather than unconstrained construction from scratch.
SU/SC records that individual skills are revised inside a maintained collection.

papers.claim_boundary: Tool schema and harness must be fixed; results do not isolate skill discovery from repair.

evidence.claim: The pipeline has Contrastive Causal Extraction, Assessment-Augmented Evolution and Topology-Aware Task Execution stages.
SpreadsheetBench-Verified is split into 200 evolution and 200 held-out samples; DocVQA uses a disjoint evolution/evaluation partition.
The paper reports WikiTableQuestions OOD and cross-model evaluations.
SU + SC separates patch quality from collection topology and routing.

papers.claim_boundary: Final score is composite evidence; extraction, assessment and routing gains require separate ablations for method-level comparison.

papers.carrier: multi-file directed graph with routing table, references and history

evidence.claim: The paper explicitly models a skill as a multi-file directed graph of a routing table and references.
The production setting contains six cloud-service categories, nine production skills and 98 skill-reference files; tickets are chronologically partitioned into four subsets.
Evolution uses multi-turn user simulation and reports fact consistency, structural consistency, regression and bloat controls.
W denotes persistent interaction and governance history; it is not claimed as a raw-memory benchmark by the authors.

papers.claim_boundary: A continual governance setting with proprietary production data; it is not directly comparable to single-turn public-benchmark rewriting.

papers.carrier: task/domain skill containing prose, scripts and references

evidence.claim: The output is a reusable skill artifact authored through a meta-skill in a CLI-agent interface without model-weight retraining.
SkillsBench uses an 83-task subset across professional domains, while KernelBench contains three GPU-kernel optimization tasks.
The protocol reports bounded exploration and validation trials and separates training variants from validation artifacts.
No non-SkillEvolver baseline is reported for the KernelBench cell.

papers.claim_boundary: SkillsBench and KernelBench are separate cells with different metrics and baseline coverage; they cannot be collapsed into one performance number.

evidence.claim: A single auditable skill is synthesized from successful and failed trajectories and evaluated through paired with-skill/without-skill intervention.
ALFWorld valid_seen is treated as IOD with overlapping task types, while valid_unseen is treated as OOD with novel task types.
The protocol separates construction verification from held-out testing and can deprecate a rejected or harmful skill.
Accepted candidates can still create held-out regressions, so repair and regression must be reported separately.

papers.claim_boundary: IOD and OOD cells support different strengths of generalization claim.

papers.carrier: loadable skill bundle plus persistent decision history

evidence.claim: The paper treats skills as loadable bundles of procedures, scripts, references and output conventions and adds persistent decision history.
Evaluation uses GAIA validation and WebWalkerQA-EN; development uses 20 disjoint WebShaper items.
Curated-search and raw-open-web settings use different search stacks, while raw-open-web systems share a portable skill-bundle interface.
SU/SC + W separates the loadable bundle, any collection behavior and the decision-history state.

papers.claim_boundary: Search stack and controller/executor configuration are major confounders; cross-setting scores are not clean skill-only comparisons.

evidence.claim: A frozen target agent is adapted by bounded add/delete/replace edits to a single skill document, accepted through a held-out gate.
The evaluation spans six benchmarks, seven target models and three execution modes.
Train, selection and test splits have distinct roles and the test split is used only for final reporting.
Cross-model, cross-harness and cross-benchmark transfer are reported as separate experiments.

papers.claim_boundary: The six benchmarks are heterogeneous evaluation cells, not samples from one homogeneous task distribution.

evidence.claim: The primary output is a hierarchical skill library with topology, atomic extraction and abstract induction.
ALFWorld uses 140 seen and 134 unseen tasks; ScienceWorld uses 194 seen and 211 unseen variations across 24 task types.
The library is constructed from training splits and no model fine-tuning is part of the stated method.
SC captures the collection-level objective; hierarchical and topology-aware are attributes rather than separate ontologies.

papers.claim_boundary: Supports collection organization and environment-internal transfer. Multi-environment evaluation is not automatically cross-environment transfer unless the same learned collection crosses environments.

evidence.claim: The paper studies 55,315 public skills and defines skills as pre-packaged instruction sets.
Controlled evaluation covers 600 skills and compares no-skill, original-skill and compressed-skill conditions.
SkillsBench evaluation covers 87 tasks, and transfer is tested across five models from four families and another agent framework.
The primary track is compression/retention, even though the artifacts being compressed can be individual skills or collections.

papers.claim_boundary: Primary outcomes are token reduction, functional retention and runtime cost, not skill discovery quality.

evidence.claim: The method co-evolves a hierarchical skill bank containing general and task-specific skills with an updated policy.
Evaluation covers ALFWorld, WebShop and seven search-QA datasets; the reported bank grows from 55 to 100 skills.
ALFWorld general skills are intended to apply across task types within the environment, while search QA distinguishes in-domain and OOD datasets.
SC + PP makes both collection growth and policy learning explicit.

papers.claim_boundary: Cannot be directly ranked against frozen external collections without isolating policy-update compute and inference context.

evidence.claim: The method synthesizes robust reusable APIs from website exploration and maintains a growing API library.
WebArena has 812 tasks across five application domains; Online-Mind2Web has 300 tasks across 136 websites, while the reported online subset uses four websites and 57 tasks.
WebArena uses automated functional correctness while real-website success is manually judged.
The artifacts are labeled executable skills/APIs because their role spans both procedural skill and generated tool interface.

papers.claim_boundary: WebArena and real-website results use different evaluators and must remain separate cells.

evidence.claim: SkillX constructs a plug-and-play knowledge base with planning, functional and atomic skill levels.
BFCL-v3 uses 50 training and 150 test items; AppWorld uses 90 training instances and Test Normal; tau2-Bench uses domain-specific train/test data.
Skills are retrieved from the initial query and evaluated with Avg@4, Pass@4 and Pass@1 across benchmarks with different tool schemas and interaction modes.
SC + KB preserves that some levels are procedural while others also encode declarative environment/tool knowledge.

papers.claim_boundary: Metrics and tool schemas differ across benchmarks; pooled averages are breadth summaries rather than one matched task distribution.

evidence.claim: SkVM treats skills as code and LLMs as heterogeneous processors and introduces a compilation/runtime system.
Experiments cover multiple models and three harnesses, including BareAgent, OpenCode and OpenClaw, with multiple generated inputs per task.
Primary measures include task completion, tokens and latency on a specified Mac Mini M4 setup.
RT marks runtime/compiler evolution rather than acquisition of new procedural knowledge.

papers.claim_boundary: Should be compared on portability and efficiency, not placed in a skill-quality leaderboard based only on success rate.

papers.carrier: filesystem directory with SKILL.md and resources

evidence.claim: A skill is formalized as a human-readable directory with a root SKILL.md and auxiliary references, scripts or assets, used by a fixed LLM agent.
SpreadsheetBench-Verified is split into 200 evolution problems and 200 held-out evaluation problems.
Additional evaluations cover artifact-disjoint and OOD transfer, including table, document and mathematical settings and cross-model reuse.
SC/consolidated directory records many-to-one consolidation without assuming every file is an independently addressable skill.

papers.claim_boundary: Some reported transfer is within-domain artifact-disjoint rather than cross-domain; the exact source-target relation must be named per cell.

papers.carrier: evolved metric plus skill lifecycle state

evidence.claim: The paper co-evolves an evaluator metric and a skill loop while keeping test held out and locked.
The protocol uses MBPP+, Spider 2.0-Snow and reference-free report generation, with a small anchored development set and an independent outer audit.
Removing anchors can cause metric collapse or Goodhart-style failure.
EV is the primary target because evaluator reliability is the central outcome, even though skills co-evolve.

papers.claim_boundary: Agent final accuracy alone is insufficient; evaluator retention, anchor generalization and reward-hacking evidence are required.

papers.carrier: persistent wiki plus filesystem skill directories

evidence.claim: Raw execution experience, accumulated wiki knowledge and executable filesystem skills are distinct states in the method.
The lifecycle includes validation gating and rollback so rejected skill updates do not erase accumulated wiki knowledge.
Evaluation spans five benchmarks and five models and includes cross-model transfer.
W→SU/SC represents memory-to-skill compilation and subsequent collection maintenance.

papers.claim_boundary: The contribution of persistent wiki state must be separated from the contribution of the final compiled skill.

evidence.claim: SKILL-KD uses teacher-student execution traces to select and distil actionable skill rules.
Teacher-only and student-only baselines score 58.3 and 60.1; pairwise and batch converge at ~59.
SKILL-KD achieves 66.8 avg score with only 38 distilled rules (3,010 words) — 58% of batch.
Pairwise produces a longer library (6,966 words) than batch (3,849 words) but with fewer rules.
Case-specific drift is handled via trace-linked edits rather than cumulative rule changes.
SKILL-KD distills to actionable rule patches rather than logits or hidden representations.

papers.claim_boundary: Supports contrastive skill distillation from teacher-student trajectories with drift-aware rule assembly. It does not by itself establish skill-collection scaling, retrieval quality, or cross-skill transfer.
